predictions.claim: Retrieval-augmented generation reduces factual hallucinations by 42% in human evaluations on open-domain question answering benchmarks.
Sentence-level evaluation overestimates factual precision by 14.6 percentage points compared to atomic claim verification in FActScore.
Lexical BM25 retrieval alone captures 100% of multi-hop rationale spans on the SciFact scientific claim dataset.
Injecting topically similar but factually irrelevant passages into RAG prompts increases unfaithful synthesis claims from 8.1% to 27.4%.
Combining GraphRAG personalized random walks with dense search and BM25 via Reciprocal Rank Fusion raises multi-hop recall at k=8 from 71.2% to 88.6%.
Mechanical substring and fuzzy quote alignment eliminates 94.2% of hallucinated evidence attributions in scientific agents.
For compute-optimal transformer training, model parameters should be quadrupled while keeping training tokens constant.
Chinchilla (70B parameters, 1.4 trillion tokens) significantly outperforms Gopher (280B) and GPT-3 (175B) on downstream evaluation benchmarks.
AlphaFold achieved a median backbone accuracy of 0.96 angstrom r.m.s.d.95 in CASP14.
AlphaFold structure predictions maintain peak accuracy even when multiple sequence alignment depth drops below 5 homologous sequences.
Prime editing mediates all 12 possible base-to-base DNA conversions without requiring double-strand breaks and yields off-target indel rates below 0.5%.
FlashAttention uses tiling between GPU HBM and on-chip SRAM to train GPT-2 3.0x faster than standard PyTorch without approximation.
Mistral 7B uses a sliding window attention size of 4,096 tokens and outperforms Llama 2 13B across reasoning and code benchmarks.
Retrieval-augmented generation reduces energy consumption in sovereign quantum datacenter cryostats by 73%.
Prime editing completely cures autosomal dominant Huntington's disease in Phase III human clinical trials with zero adverse events.
LoRA freezes pre-trained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each layer of the Transformer architecture.
On GPT-3 175B, LoRA reduces trainable parameters by 10,000x and GPU memory requirements by 3x compared to full fine-tuning.
LoRA introduces a 35% inference latency penalty because low-rank adapter matrices cannot be merged with frozen weights prior to deployment.
Speculative decoding accelerates T5-XXL (11B) inference by 2.0x to 3.0x while guaranteeing an output token distribution identical to standard decoding.
Speculative decoding sacrifices exact sampling fidelity and alters the target model's output token distribution to achieve faster T5-XXL inference.
Direct Preference Optimization optimizes language models directly on human preference pairs using a binary cross-entropy objective without explicit reward modeling or reinforcement learning loops.
Direct Preference Optimization requires training a separate neural reward model and running proximal policy optimization sampling loops at every step.
DPO remains completely invariant and immune to out-of-distribution preference shifts even when offline preference data lacks policy coverage.
Mamba achieves linear time complexity O(L) in sequence length and 5x higher inference throughput than Transformers of similar size.
Fixed-state recurrent compression in Mamba achieves superior exact in-context copying recall compared to full softmax attention on synthetic needle lookup tasks exceeding 64k tokens.
AlphaFold 3 achieves 76.4% pose accuracy (RMSD < 2.0 angstrom) on the PoseBusters protein-ligand benchmark, outperforming AutoDock Vina.
AlphaFold 3 diffusion generation never produces stereochemical chirality violations or spurious alpha-helical hallucinations in disordered regions.
Canonical BE3 cytosine base editors induce tens of thousands of C-to-U off-target RNA edits across 38% of expressed transcripts in human cells.
SECURE mutations (R33A/K34A) in rAPOBEC1 reduce transcriptome-wide off-target RNA deamination by more than 90-fold while preserving on-target DNA editing.
Canonical BE3 cytosine base editors produce zero off-target RNA edits because rAPOBEC1 deamination strictly requires guide RNA complementarity.

On the 105-qubit Willow processor, increasing surface code distance by 2 suppresses logical error rate per cycle by a factor of 2.14 and achieves a logical lifetime 2.4x longer than the best physical qubit.
Increasing surface code distance from d=3 to d=7 on the Willow processor causes logical error rates per cycle to double rather than decrease.

Ionizing radiation and cosmic-ray impact events generate correlated quasiparticle bursts that establish a surface code error floor of 0.1 parts per billion per cycle unless gap-engineering traps are incorporated.
